shared.body: K-series keys open restricted rooms, including Personnel File Room 417. A K-series key may be withdrawn only for an assigned task, with the duty manager's authorization given before the withdrawal and recorded on a key authorization form signed by the duty manager. The key may be used only to enter rooms the task requires. Papers in Room 417 may be handled only by Personnel Office staff, except to protect them from immediate damage.

Priya Halloran phoned me at about ten to seven about water on floor 4 east and asked for K-14, which covers 417, 419 and 421. I approved it on the phone and told her to go ahead. I sign the authorization forms for evening calls when I get in the next morning, so I signed this one at 08:20 on the 26th. I did not ask which rooms she would need.

facts.statement: At 18:41 on 25 February 2026 the Operations desk took a call from night custodian Tobiah Wren about water on the fourth-floor east corridor.
At 18:44 Operations operator Gail Fenwick dispatched Halloran by service request SR-4471 to check and isolate a ceiling drip on the fourth-floor east corridor.
Halloran's key-cabinet PIN is enrolled for restricted key K-14.
K-14 opens Rooms 417, 419 and 421 on the fourth floor east: the Personnel File Room, the east plumbing riser closet and the Records Manager's office.
SR-4471 gave the drip's location as the corridor between Rooms 417 and 419 and named neither room as the source.
The Room 417 door contact recorded the door open from 19:12 to 19:38.
Duty manager Marcus Ebdon signed key authorization form KA-0225-3 for K-14 at 08:20 on 26 February, after the key had been withdrawn and returned.
At 18:49, before the withdrawal, Ebdon approved Halloran's request for K-14 by phone.
For evening key requests Ebdon gives his approval by phone and signs the authorization form when he arrives the next morning.
At 18:52 Halloran withdrew K-14 from key cabinet KC-2 with her PIN.
Halloran returned K-14 to key cabinet KC-2 at 20:06.
Halloran is an applicant for the Senior Building Engineer vacancy, selection BE-26-04.
On the evening of 25 February the BE-26-04 panel folder, holding nine scoring sheets, was in Personnel specialist Lorna Specht's in-tray in Room 417.
Before 19:12 the Room 417 door was last closed at 17:05, when the Personnel Office staff left for the day.
At 08:30 on 26 February the key cabinet's daily exception check flagged K-14 because its authorization form was signed after the withdrawal.
At 09:40 on 26 February Specht annotated the exception to say that Room 417 holds the BE-26-04 files and that Halloran is an applicant.
Halloran went first to riser closet 419, arriving at 18:58.
From 19:50 to 20:02 Halloran mopped the fourth-floor east corridor.
On 23 February Halloran replaced a light fitting in Room 417 under work order WO-6087, using K-14.
A cracked condensate drain line above the Room 417 ceiling leaked water onto shelving bay 3 and through the corridor ceiling outside the room.
In the 18:41 call Wren reported water coming out under the door of Room 417.
Halloran entered Room 417 to deal with the water coming through its ceiling onto shelving bay 3.
In Room 417 Halloran lifted six file boxes off the wet shelf onto a table, took down two soaked ceiling tiles and set out buckets.
In riser closet 419 Halloran closed the drain-line isolation valve at 19:03, which slowed the leak.
At 19:46 Halloran phoned the Operations desk and reported the drain-line leak over Room 417, the closed valve and the six moved boxes.
Work order WO-6120 of 26 February records the cracked drain line above Room 417 replaced, four ceiling tiles replaced and six file boxes released to the Personnel Office for drying.
Halloran did not open any file box or touch the papers on the desks in Room 417.
After a 16:52 job by Specht, the Room 417 copier logged no further jobs on 25 February.
A loose cleanout cap on the drain stack in riser closet 419 leaked water that dripped through the corridor ceiling outside 419.
No water reached Room 417 on 25 February.
In the 18:41 call Wren reported water on the corridor floor outside riser closet 419.
In riser closet 419 Halloran tightened the loose cleanout cap and set a bucket under it, finishing at 19:09.
Halloran found Room 417 dry within a minute of entering at 19:12 and had no work there for the rest of her time inside, until 19:38.
Halloran used K-14 to enter Room 417 and read the nine BE-26-04 panel scoring sheets in Specht's in-tray.
Halloran wanted to see how the BE-26-04 panel had scored her before the selection decision due on 4 March.
After 19:09 Halloran was alone in the fourth-floor east suite with K-14 still signed out to her.
At 19:24 Halloran made nine walk-up copies on the Room 417 copier and took the copies with her.
On 23 February, while replacing the light fitting in Room 417, Halloran saw the BE-26-04 panel folder in Specht's in-tray.
At 19:46 Halloran phoned the Operations desk and reported only the cleanout cap tightened in riser closet 419.
Work order WO-6120 of 26 February records the cleanout cap gasket in riser closet 419 replaced and the Room 417 ceiling and shelving inspected and found dry.
The Room 417 copier logged a nine-page walk-up copy job at 19:24 on 25 February.

A building engineer takes a restricted suite key for a leak call whose dispatch names no single room, then spends 26 minutes in the personnel file room that holds a selection she has applied for; the duty manager signs the key form the next morning.
